body.section: 三人36客户完整SPE的聚合末位保底反例

input_binding.task_queue_state_scope: Claimed or normally delivered done is accepted; queue stage is not a mathematical premise. Owner, definition identity, frozen-source hashes and registered body bindings remain checked.
input_binding.formula_translation: Source-bound hand translation of the complete 36-customer formula policy and all-n equations (2),(3),(5); no repository solver or prior numeric report is imported.

small_36_customer_example.scope: One source-bound fixed 36-unit-customer instance and the original formula complete pure SPE; all-p follows analytically after the finite replay.
small_36_customer_example.complete_formula_policy: root 0; after (a), smallest label of opposite group; after (a,b), smallest unused label in b's group, including repeated/off-path histories.
all_p_proof: For each i the actual action z_i is one legal column and, after the original actual prefix z_<i, the same fixed complete policy returns Z_i(z_i)=z.
Thus for every probability vector p on the six original labels, R_i(p)=min_A sum_T p_T K_i(T,A) <= sum_T p_T Q_T(z). This chooses one action before T is drawn and never exchanges min and expectation.
Summing the three inequalities gives sum_i R_i(p) <= 3 sum_T p_T Q_T(z) <= 3 max_T Q_T(z)=57/2 < W=34. This is uniform over the whole probability simplex; zero query distributions are enumerated.

all_n_family_n6_regression.scope: A finite n=6 arithmetic regression of the original all-n K=6M+4 family; the analytic all-n argument is separate.

input_formula.F: 1 for a pure-group n-subset, -1 for a mixed (n-1)-subset, 0 otherwise; F(empty)=0
input_formula.x_B: sum_(A superset B) (-1)^(|A|-|B|) z_A for B nonempty

all_n_family_n6_regression.actual_terminal_policy_source: The source formula takes root X0, then Y0, then fresh labels of the second label's Y group. Only this path is evaluated here.
all_n_family_n6_regression.theta_scope: K*b+1 is evaluated from the original theorem. Exact minimization over all repeated n-1 backgrounds is not enumerated; the original repeated-background splitting proof supplies equality to theta_n.
all_n_family_n6_regression.tight_bound_numeric_verification: All six unused labels have signed query 0 and total query K*beta; all six used labels have strictly smaller direct positive-type queries. Thus this n=6 type table has max_T Q_T(z)=K*beta, checked independently by coefficient integrals.
all_n_family_n6_regression.all_p_budget_bridge: For the original fixed complete compiled SPE, choose the actual action in each row, giving R_i(p)<=E_p Q_T(z). The all-type uniform query contribution is at most beta, while the signed contribution is at most M in absolute value. Therefore sum_i R_i(p)<=n(K beta+M)=U<W for every p. The finite script checks n=6 constants; the proof for every n>=3 is separate.
all_n_family_n6_regression.full_SPE_legality_scope: The existing analytic compiler and the source auxiliary complete distinct-history policy establish a full original SPE, including all repeated off-path histories. This program recomputes exact quantities and neither builds nor exhaustively certifies that enormous complete strategy.

execution.started_and_completed_invocations_scope: This count increments on every successful invocation preserving the sibling report; no hidden solver or prior report is executed.
execution.write_scope: Only the sibling budget-example-results.json; source files and all shared registries/edges/receipts are read-only.

conclusion_limits: The two explicit source-bound examples have a uniform all-p SUMmin-full budget bound; this is not a proof of general SUMmin-full.
The 36-customer formula policy agrees at all 43 nodes with its own original frozen certificate. It is not replaced by the separate onpath_budget_failure policy used in the older finite-query report.
The n=6 arithmetic regression checks 4095 positive interest types in compressed form, not a unit expansion, not a complete SPE enumeration, and not an all-n computational proof.
Both aggregate-theta counterexamples remain counterexamples to W>=n theta_n, and neither is a half-coverage counterexample.
